theme: 3 SwiftUI terms for sizing and placing views around their container

terms.definition: A row inside a Grid that places its views in columns.
terms.example: Put each pair of labels in a GridRow.

terms.definition: A modifier that adds a view at an edge and moves the content out of its way.
terms.example: Add the player bar with safeAreaInset.

terms.definition: A modifier that sizes a view as a share of its container, such as a scroll view.
terms.example: Use containerRelativeFrame to make each card 80 percent wide.

video.title: GridRow, safeAreaInset & containerRelativeFrame | Day 179
video.description:
Learn to explain how to size views by their container and add bars at the edge in SwiftUI: GridRow, safeAreaInset & containerRelativeFrame, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
GridRow - A row inside a Grid that places its views in columns.
safeAreaInset - A modifier that adds a view at an edge and moves the content out of its way.
containerRelativeFrame - A modifier that sizes a view as a share of its container, such as a scroll view.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain GridRow, safeAreaInset & containerRelativeFrame in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

GridRow - A row inside a Grid that places its views in columns.
한국어: 그리드로우: Grid 안에서 뷰들을 열에 맞춰 배치하는 행

safeAreaInset - A modifier that adds a view at an edge and moves the content out of its way.
한국어: 세이프에어리어인셋: 가장자리에 뷰를 더하고 콘텐츠를 그 자리에서 비켜 주는 모디파이어

containerRelativeFrame - A modifier that sizes a view as a share of its container, such as a scroll view.
한국어: 컨테이너릴레이티브프레임: 스크롤 뷰 같은 컨테이너의 일부 비율로 뷰 크기를 정하는 모디파이어

landscape.hook: Can you explain GridRow, safeAreaInset and containerRelativeFrame in English?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I want a footer bar that does not cover my list.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use safeAreaInset on the list, with `edge: .bottom`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So safeAreaInset moves the content out of the way?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, the list gets shorter, and the footer sits below it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. Now my cards are too wide on iPad.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use containerRelativeFrame. It sizes a card by its container.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can containerRelativeFrame make it 80 percent wide?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used a fixed width before, and it broke on small screens.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A relative size fixes that. Now, how do you align the labels?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I put them in a Grid, and each pair goes in a GridRow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. A GridRow makes the labels line up in columns.
Put each pair of labels in a GridRow.
